passage:
When the results went up, Samir's name sat at the very top of the engineering batch list. He read it three times, then ran across the quad to find Sabina.

"Top of the batch!" he said, out of breath.

Sabina's smile arrived a second late. "Wow. Should I start calling you Professor now?" A couple of people laughed. Samir's grin folded in on itself and he mumbled that he had to go.

That night Sabina lay awake with one thought looping: he got there and I am still waiting. She loved him, and envy sat in her chest right beside the love, and both were true. She wrote it on the back of her notebook, just for herself. Then, plainly, she wrote what she wanted from her own project this year.

Samir, meanwhile, had phoned Kalyani, who whooped so loudly he held the phone away from his ear, and it warmed him.

Next morning Sabina found him at the tea stall. "That joke was mean, and I'm sorry. I'm really proud of you. Also a bit jealous, honestly." Samir studied her face. "Thanks for saying it. Next time, just say the jealous part." She bought the tea. 🙂

qa.q: Where did Samir's name appear on the results?
qa.a: It sat at the very top of the engineering batch list.

qa.q: How did Sabina's private feelings connect to the coldness Samir met when he shared his news?
qa.a: Sabina's envy, sitting beside her love for him, came out as a teasing joke that made Samir's excitement fold. Once she named the envy privately and then said it kindly, she could celebrate, while Samir had already found cheering from Kalyani.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling when Sabina made the Professor joke?
qa.a: He felt hurt and deflated; his grin folded in and he hurried away.

qa.q: What could Samir do next time good news is met with a cold joke?
qa.a: He could tell the person kindly how it landed, as he did at the tea stall, and keep sharing his wins with people like Kalyani who cheer.

grounding: Shows envy of a partner's success from the partner who feels smaller and covers it with a joke, and from the partner whose good news is met with coldness.
